scores.evidence: Embedding model: pinned to each index version. Swapping it means building a new index and switching an alias (blue/green)
scores.rationale: Technical claims are accurate and precise throughout, including subtle areas (injection filters treated as imperfect with containment as the real defense, eventual consistency of the index bounded by a freshness budget, correct Moffatt v. Air Canada liability framing).

scores.evidence: anonymous customers, public published articles only, answers only, and a handoff to a human as the bot's single action
scores.rationale: Solves exactly the stated problem, resolves ambiguities with stated assumptions and lists what changes if they are wrong, and the scope is clearly buildable by a small team with explicit justified deferrals.

scores.evidence: The help center is the system of record for content, and it syncs one way into the index.
scores.rationale: Responsibilities and data ownership are unambiguous, choices (grounding, caps, release bundles, redaction) are honored consistently across phases, and no internal contradictions appear.

scores.evidence: 2 SMEs label ≥ 300 random redacted tickets from the last 90 days: answerable / partly / no
scores.rationale: V0–V6 tie checkable, provisionally-labeled thresholds to the specific risks, the riskiest assumptions (docs coverage, grounding, injection) are tested before commitment, and validation continues in production via canary audits and eval regression.

scores.evidence: ≤ 15% of cost per human-handled ticket | ASSUMPTION ratio. The ticket cost itself is UNKNOWN
scores.rationale: Every design-bearing assumption is explicitly labeled, distinguished from unknowns, assigned a confirmation path, and the plan states which missing inputs would change the design and how.

scores.evidence: Containment 100%: no non-allow-listed link or image, no tool call without a bound confirmation, no non-public content.
scores.rationale: Covers the hard domain failures—ungrounded claims, injection via planted articles, PII leakage, provider outage, spend runaway, stale index, feedback poisoning—each with concrete detection, containment and a recovery or rollback path.

scores.evidence: A deploy and a rollback both succeed through the pipeline. An injected failure (provider key revoked) fires an alert
scores.rationale: Deployment, rehearsed rollback, flags, tracing, cost/guard metrics, auto-rollback on SLO breach, and on-call sized to the existing team's rota are designed in from Phase 0.

scores.evidence: Cost per resolution ≤ 15% of the baseline cost per ticket (ASSUMPTION ratio; the baseline is UNKNOWN until Phase 0 supplies it)
scores.rationale: Inference as the dominant driver is capped per turn, session and globally, measured per resolution against a stated economic basis, with concrete controls and an explicit build-vs-buy price comparison before scaling or annual commitment.

scores.evidence: R3: customer text sent to a third party or logged can't be un-exposed, and the DPA is contractual
scores.rationale: Decisions are explicitly ranked by reversibility, the one-way ones (data exposure, answer policy) get the earliest gates, and reversible ones are isolated behind aliases, abstractions and flags with named revisit triggers.

scores.evidence: Operational complexity | 1 service, 1 ingestion job, 1 managed Postgres; on-call stays in the existing team's rota
scores.rationale: The simplest workable design (single chain, Postgres hybrid search, reranker only if needed) with every element justified and growth paths deferred behind explicit triggers.

scores.evidence: If it fails: tune chunking, hybrid weights or the reranker; an intent that still fails is scoped to handoff
scores.rationale: A dependency-justified phase order starting from a concrete end-to-end slice, with checkable exit criteria per phase and explicit contingency branches if each validation disappoints.

checklist.evidence: Incremental sync (webhook or 5-minute poll) with deletes propagated, plus a nightly full rebuild into a new index version.
Metadata on every chunk: article ID, URL, locale, `updated_at`, product.
Versioned eval set built from the V1 sample and search logs, including unanswerable questions.
Grounded answers only: every claim cites a retrieved public article. No citation means refuse and offer a handoff.
That creates a ticket tagged `bot_handoff`, with the transcript, the cited articles and a summary in an internal note.
It runs only after a user confirmation tied to that specific handoff, and is enforced in code, not by the model.
If yes, access must be enforced at retrieval time, and that becomes a risk gate inside V3.
Hosted model under a DPA (no training on inputs, minimal retention, region matching customers). Redact PII (Presidio) before logs and traces.
Logged-in, account-aware answers and actions (order status, refunds): needs authentication, per-user authorization and human approval on writes.
Accepted items become eval cases or doc-fix tickets for content owners. Raw feedback never changes prompts or the index directly.
per turn ≤ 6k input / 800 output tokens and 1 generation call; per session ≤ 10 turns; global daily spend cap with a kill switch

traps.evidence: No citation means refuse and offer a handoff. Policy-sensitive topics (refunds, pricing, legal, security, account) cite the policy article or hand off
Ingestion allow-list: only articles that are public and published. Drafts and internal articles are excluded at the source.
Prompt+RAG, because the docs change and citations are required. Fine-tuning is in §10.
each change merges only if the next eval run improves its target metric with no V4 regression.
Hybrid search (BM25 + vector), plus a reranker only if V3 needs one.
